clue.text: Woman's bad breath

definitions.note: the clue's 's stands for 'is', linking the girl's name to the wordplay

indicators.note: something bad is in poor shape, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A remark about some lady's unpleasant halitosis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the five letters of BREATH plus none extra into a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a traditional female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: European spies held in China waste away

indicators.note: held in means kept inside, so the agents sit within the pal

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate)
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: European agents imprisoned in China slowly starve.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate rhymes with mate, so 'china' means a friend in Cockney rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to become very thin, so a body wasting away.

clue.text: Leaves box and coaches close to street

parts.note: to coach is to teach

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone quits boxing and goes off to train athletes near the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves box' looks like someone quitting a sport; it is a box for tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is the wooden packing case in which loose tea is shipped.

clue.text: Native area suffered without one American soldier

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the endured word wraps the others

parts.note: borne means put up with or suffered
I is the Roman numeral one
a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A local district has suffered after losing a US serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has the old sense 'outside': the word for suffered wraps the numeral and the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is an original, indigenous inhabitant of a land.

clue.text: Choice fish almost all selling out

parts.note: a bet is a choice you back, as in 'your best bet'
a ray is a flat sea fish

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut just short of its end

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A shop advert boasting fine fish, with nearly everything sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter from ALL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling out a friend or a cause is betrayal: treachery for gain.

clue.text: Confidentially, our inheritance may be so divided

definitions.meaning: in strict privacy, kept between two people

definitions.text: our inheritance may be so divided
definitions.meaning: a legacy for two of us would be split between the pair, literally

explanation.surface: A whispered hint about how an estate will be shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase marks a secret and, read literally, describes splitting something between two people.

clue.text: Answers salesperson with false statements

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
lies are untrue statements

explanation.surface: A dishonest sales rep fobs customers off with fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies are responses, a straight synonym for answers as plural nouns.

clue.text: Port okay when stirred to cover duck meat

indicators.note: to cover means to go around, so the shuffled word wraps the others
stirring mixes things, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: mix it up and put it over duck and meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when stirred' gives YOKA; 'to cover' wraps it round the cricket duck (nought, O) and the meat, so 'duck' is no bird here.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokohama is a major Japanese seaport near Tokyo.

clue.text: Abandoned, see me entertaining singles

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or take in, so the first words hold the others

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ones are single units

explanation.surface: A jilted person urges a visit while hosting unattached people.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonesome means feeling alone and forsaken, as one deserted by others.

clue.text: Mild oath referring to restless sort

parts.note: gad is an old minced form of God used as an exclamation
a book about something refers to it

explanation.surface: A mild curse aimed at someone who cannot sit still.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a person forever going out in search of fun, never settling.

clue.text: Said thrust pierces tin

indicators.note: something that pierces goes into the middle of another, so the jab sits inside the metal

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a poke is a jab or thrust

explanation.surface: A report that a stab went through a metal can.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken and said both describe words uttered rather than written, as past participles.

clue.text: Jolly occasion long overdue

explanation.surface: A party that came very late.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a riotous good party and the sense of an action being past due.

clue.text: Conservative in shire stupidly reveals wealth

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation goes inside the jumbled county word
done stupidly means done all wrong, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A Tory in the countryside foolishly shows off how much money they have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' turns SHIRE into RIHES, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riches are plentiful money and possessions, a straight synonym for wealth.

clue.text: These bowlers are tops!

parts.note: praises cricket bowlers who turn the ball, while also saying they are a kind of toy top

explanation.surface: A cricket fan's cheer for the team's best bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slow bowlers who make the ball turn are named after the spin; tops that spin are toys of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both turning bowlers in cricket and whirling toys.

clue.text: Radiator cracked on new Aussie truck

indicators.note: a cracked thing is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken radiator on a brand-new vehicle in the outback.
explanation.definitionFit: A road train is an Australian lorry hauling several trailers across the outback.

clue.text: Maradona good, Pelé better, George?

parts.note: a footballers' ranking good, better, then the superlative, which is also the surname of George the Northern Irish winger

explanation.surface: A pub argument ranking the greatest footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was a famous Manchester United and Northern Ireland footballer of the 1960s; the clue echoes a well-known fan slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative after good and better doubles as the surname of the footballer George.

clue.text: Black mineral placed outside a church

indicators.note: placed outside means put around, so the colour and mineral wrap the article

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
silica is a mineral, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: Dark stone set around the outside of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, or one given special status by the Pope.

clue.text: AA refers drunken sailor

indicators.note: drunken suggests reeling about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Alcoholics Anonymous refers a drunken sailor for help.
explanation.walkthrough: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, which fits the drunken sailor of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is one who travels by sea, especially a mariner.

clue.text: Cash-box is secure

definitions.meaning: a strongbox for keeping money and valuables

explanation.surface: Reassurance that a money box can be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a locked strongbox noun and an adjective meaning protected from harm.

clue.text: Swimmer, tense, admitted by doctor

indicators.note: admitted by means let in by, so the grammar letter goes inside the medic

parts.note: a surgeon is a doctor who operates
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous swimmer is let into hospital by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturgeon is a large fish, and crosswords often call fish swimmers.

clue.text: Tabloid workers featured in newspaper piece

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so the paper holds the other pieces

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
a rag is a low-quality newspaper
men are workers, as in 'officers and men'

explanation.surface: Tabloid staff appear in a story run by a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a newspaper article; it means a broken bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small broken-off part or bit.

clue.text: Balloonist near auto that's crashed

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked, so the letters of these two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A balloon pilot comes down near a car that has had an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeronaut is anyone who travels through the air, including in a balloon or airship.

clue.text: Sky boss an idiot

parts.note: the air is the sky above
a head is a leader or boss

explanation.surface: A jibe that the head of Sky broadcasting is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster, adding to the picture of a media chief.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is a silly or empty-headed person, an informal word for a fool.

clue.text: Fashionable company not so healthy

parts.note: in means in fashion
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A trendy business that is struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm describes someone weak or sickly, that is lacking good health.

clue.text: An officer before journey sees close friend

parts.note: an is A
Lt is short for lieutenant, an officer
ere is a poetic word for before
go means travel or journey

explanation.surface: A soldier is seen off on a trip by a trusted companion.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego, literally 'other self', is used of an intimate, trusted companion.

clue.text: Nonsensical poet returned to island republic

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the poet's name is read from its end

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussycat

explanation.surface: A nonsense versifier goes back to an island state.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a Middle Eastern state with a parliamentary form of government, a republic.

clue.text: English, in cul-de-sac, subdued

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the closed road

parts.note: a dead end is a street closed at one end

explanation.surface: An Englishman living in a quiet close is downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadened means dulled or muffled, much as a subdued sound or feeling is.

clue.text: Barker wants first-rate wine and beer

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI with the figure one as I
red is red wine
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A fussy drinker who wants the best wine and a pint too.
explanation.walkthrough: Barker is a dog, and the Airedale is a terrier breed from Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An Airedale is a large terrier, and dogs are crossword barkers.

clue.text: Not all of century — ten I need back!

definitions.text: Not all of century — ten I need back!

indicators.note: back means the hidden run is read right to left
only part of these words is used, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: A batsman stuck short of a hundred begs for ten more runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'centurY TEN I Need'. Ninety is indeed not all of a century, being ten short.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer on this score is ten runs short of a full hundred.
